rounds.notes:
## ROUND ONE IS A VITAL ROUND
You need to earn 11k for the next round. Bonus points (literally) if you can get 11.5k. Squeeze out all the juices you can this round. Getting 11k isn't super hard, but not getting it means you'll be very behind round two. The better you are at weaving, the more likely you will be to reach that number so you should practice it

## UNDERSTAND THE DIFFERENCE IN PLAYSTYLES!
There are three routes for one round. If you don't want to use [Clone Conjuration](item_6c9f6be1-ab29-4f46-af24-34e4835f9af3), then take [Fleet Foot](item_1d58371c-71a9-44c2-8d5a-0663467599e9) or [Two-Zu](item_80f16d3e-a4c0-4fa8-90b1-a0f033a1a77b)

If you take [Clone Conjuration](item_6c9f6be1-ab29-4f46-af24-34e4835f9af3), you're going to be playing Kiriko exactly like you would in the core game. If you're desperate to heal your team, you have the option of tping just to spawn a clone, but be aware that your clone will have significantly weaker healing than you. This is probably the safest pick, but it comes with the downside of you not really playing a stadium build yet

If you take [Fleet Foot](item_1d58371c-71a9-44c2-8d5a-0663467599e9), you have the option of tping directly onto a backline target. ONLY DO THIS IF YOU'RE CERTAIN YOU'LL EARN THE ELIMINATION OR FORCE THEM OUT OF THE FIGHT. I usually don't take this yet because this power scales really well with [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction) and will be a surprise in the later, more important rounds. After the nerfs, it's an even worse option early on as you'll only be working to your original cooldown length with [Cooldown Reduction](stat_cooldown_reduction). This is best picked if the enemy is running something like [Ashe](hero_37b42a2d-a82d-4a22-9df2-4c812c873b54) or [Ana](hero_f1aee6cf-704f-455f-a100-ec882ebbe000) and you don't have a [Genji](hero_31fd201d-2f46-41e4-b125-9fa9e55fed46) or [Lucio](hero_b38c5d54-a585-4545-b0b8-4d4b205b3768) to pressure them. DO NOT TAKE THIS if the enemy team has a [Reaper](hero_0449752f-1c58-487b-b9a0-ca727d784457) or [Mei](hero_36fd67f0-19df-4c50-add9-709cfb147cb0). These two are your biggest opps, and even though there's the chance you'll be able to outplay them, don't gamble round one and two. Snowballs start in these rounds, they're the most vital rounds

You can also take [Two-Zu](item_80f16d3e-a4c0-4fa8-90b1-a0f033a1a77b). This becomes a more enticing pick if there's an enemy comp like [Junker Queen](hero_4794d288-27d9-49e0-a1dd-ffe0f4de3ab1), [Ana](hero_f1aee6cf-704f-455f-a100-ec882ebbe000), [Ashe](hero_37b42a2d-a82d-4a22-9df2-4c812c873b54) in round one that can put out a lot of negative effects. With this power, you can and should be more liberal with your first suzu, but try to bank your second suzu

## VICTORY ISN'T AS IMPORTANT AS PREPARING FOR ROUND THREE
You should play to win these rounds, but don't be disheartened if you lose these rounds. **Focus on staying on-track with your money**. These rounds aren't just vital because you'll have the opportunity to win on mercy rule, these rounds are vital because this is where the snowball starts. Get your bag girl (or boy or otherwise)

## THE THREE STEP PLAN
The three (four) step plan is the basic theory of how to play Kiriko. I mentioned it in the build description but if you scrolled past it, it's important for you to know
1. Take an aggressive angle during setup phase, look for high ground and a sightline on your team (optional, but be ready to tp back) and the enemy team (mandatory)
2. Deal damage from this angle until things go wrong for you OR your team
3. Teleport back (step three of the four-step plan is survive an engage with suzu but using suzu isn't as hard a rule as the others) to your team to help them stabilize and repeat

rounds.notes:
## THIS ROUND IS VITAL
Make sure you end this round with over 21k. You can end much lower than this, but the goal is to be able to afford [Hardlight Accelerator](item_0390c8af-2a68-4da2-b876-93da32c3f448) in round three without selling anything

## UNDERSTAND THE PLAYSTYLE
You now have the ability to two-tap most squishy targets with a headshot, so you can now be extremely aggressive. Hitting your headshots isn't as vital as hitting your shots in general, but if you're confident with hitting them, shoot for the head. Try not to jump a lot. You'll miss more often, and you don't want to extend your fights. Every second in a duel is a second not spent watching your team

rounds.notes:
## THIS IS A SNOWBALL ROUND
Everyone on the field gets a huge power spike this round, you included. If you've been losing the past two rounds, then try being more aggressive this round. You should aim to have 30k next round, but at this point you should play to win

## UNDERSTAND THE DIFFERENT PLAYSTYLES
If you picked [Clone Conjuration](item_6c9f6be1-ab29-4f46-af24-34e4835f9af3) or [Fleet Foot](item_1d58371c-71a9-44c2-8d5a-0663467599e9) round one, then picking the other will give you a huge power spike for this round. Clone Conjuration and Fleet Foot will help you take fights you couldn't win before. This won't save you against  [Reaper](hero_0449752f-1c58-487b-b9a0-ca727d784457) or [Mei](hero_36fd67f0-19df-4c50-add9-709cfb147cb0) but it might help against [Cassidy](hero_3dd63854-7558-4344-86e4-b506f807129b) and [Soldier: 76](hero_e1ac7ef5-4648-4998-b8b0-9e3da3e60546) if he's running a helix rockets build. You'll also be able to reset much faster after a duel

If you don't want to take clone (especially if you're a little scared after the clone nerfs), take [Self-Care](item_0b7b0332-9bf6-4905-810e-7614b914d663). The ability to heal yourself without suzu is very important and sometimes you can't get to a health pack. Health packs are still the better option but it's useful if you don't have one nearby

rounds.notes:
## STRATEGIZE
Round three is where you'll get the full picture of everyone's build. You'll know now almost exactly what to expect from your enemies and allies, and this is where you can make your judgements on what you will and will not be able to do going forward. For example, if the enemy Ashe is running a dynamite build, you can make a decision based on round three on whether or not you can dive her, in this case you should cooldown reduction this round so you can teleport onto her for an early pick and to have a very powerful angle behind the enemy team. If their reaper is constantly teleporting onto your team, you can get away with teleporting into theirs more often (especially because your teleport is faster than theirs

## Post-nerf Playstyle
Your [Fleet Foot](item_1d58371c-71a9-44c2-8d5a-0663467599e9) is now significantly slower, so you should be a lot more conservative with your tps. You're no longer the omnipresent murder monster you used to be, but you still have insane mobility. Try to take angles without using your teleport and basically use your swift step like a genji dash to either secure a kill with a new angle or to escape a bad engage

[Donut Delivery](item_296adb69-d517-4885-903a-ef8f3a1d6a7b) makes your life so much easier. You can burst heal your core and your clone will spawn in too so you'll be able to very quickly stabilize your team. I highly recommend taking this. The cooldown reduction and passive value it provides is pivotal. It might also heal you too but I'm not sure

If you don't think you'll benefit from the extra cooldown reduction (usually because mei and reapear exist and are making your life hell), go for more weapon power if you can afford it

## UNDERSTAND THE ROUND
Not all builds are fully realized by round 3 and 4, so while you had the advantage of being mostly complete versus a bunch of builds that were only a third of the way there, you've reached a soft cap on your power spiking. Not that you **don't** scale in round 5, but if you're losing by this point, you should really consider your options. It's not too late by this point to go for a healing focus. Just pick up [Ryōta’s Reloader](item_5cabe555-3845-49fa-9941-71b870c2c164). There's absolutely no reason to NOT pick [Two-Zu](item_80f16d3e-a4c0-4fa8-90b1-a0f033a1a77b) this round. No other power makes your life easier like two-zu and it's the basis for the next spike in round 7 if you make it there. As for items, stack weapon power if you already have 25% cooldown reduction. My ratio by this point is usually 25 crd to 50 wp. If you can afford [The Closer](item_173c6d0f-dbe6-440e-924f-0ce08189ddce), you should always choose that over [Eye of the Spider](item_bbaf01d7-340d-4199-b738-86a98d68fe9b), as the headshot damage will be slightly higher and that's what matters, even if you've been missing most of your headshots

## UNDERSTAND THE PLAYSTYLE
Round 5 is another very important round. Most games are settled on this round, and this is also another point where builds could scale past you (remember that even though a build might be stronger, that doesn't mean you can't beat them in a fight). Because you have such incredible kill pressure with your two-shot, you should still remain aggressive. If the enemy has an [Ashe](hero_37b42a2d-a82d-4a22-9df2-4c812c873b54), MAKE HER LIFE HELL. As you start to even out with other builds, you should try to up your aggression to compensate. This is usually the point where you will try to throw your ofuda at someone at like 80% and then they die before your ofuda reach them. Sometimes you just can't save your team with healing, so when that happens go bully the enemy

## MAJOR POST-NERF ADJUSTMENT
Because your swift step takes much longer to come online when teleporting without an ally, it could be smart to pick up [Keen Kunai](item_d5993121-8a5f-4c59-9145-19dc55265f48) this round and save [Two-Zu](item_80f16d3e-a4c0-4fa8-90b1-a0f033a1a77b) for round 7. I would still pick up Two-Zu this round, because the nerfs aren't detrimental, but it is something to consider if you've been hitting your headshots and feel like you need it

rounds.notes:
## UNDERSTAND THE ROUND
This is the round you have to start pushing your limits on. Even if you're up one, you should start playing with the absolute maximum effort and try to be as aggressive and mobile as you can manage. Don't risk a round seven, even if you're sure you'll win. There are no real changes in this round. You know from round 5 what specializations the enemy team has gone for, just stack weapon power if possible. You can also opt to pick up [Martian Mender](item_0099632b-4e18-450e-844f-22c40e51bc98). This is probably the only survivability item that matters to you, because the passive health regeneration will help you reset after a duel and the cooldown reduction is vital to this build. I wouldn't sacrifice weapon power for it, though. If you can't afford it, pick it up next round

rounds.notes:
## THE LAST ROUND
If you made it here, you're in a tight match and this round is probably going to be close. This is the round you will need to focus on doing a specific thing during step three. If your team is getting burned, anti'd, poisoned, or otherwise bullied with negative effects, pick up [Cleansing Charge](item_4721f307-30d2-4fc1-a10b-6de7141deb68). It seems silly but TRUST ME, that's up to 25% ult charge from one suzu and you'll deny the enemy team resources (and the enemy Ashe her ult charge). It's not hard to get even 15% off of one suzu, especially against an enemy team running [Cybervenom](item_210a8582-91ec-4cf3-968a-a443f3a0c505) builds. There will be so many effects for you to cleanse you'll be rolling in ult charge. Pick up [Spirit Veil](item_1772ce7d-37ed-41e4-8bac-d9b260aa59ad) if you notice you're drawing a lot of aggro. Otherwise, pick up [Keen Kunai](item_d5993121-8a5f-4c59-9145-19dc55265f48). You can also play around with the power that lowers enemy move speed but that's even more niche than [Cleansing Charge](item_4721f307-30d2-4fc1-a10b-6de7141deb68) to the point where I don't even care to memorize its name
